about: Chapter 1: she looks the organizers up online (evidence_table `screen`): a search home page, the query typed, then a full results page; generic results only. One fixed camera centre (start_center = focus + end_offset) frames the home field at the start and the results field at the top at the end, so the camera only eases back a little (3.1 to 2.8) and the query stays big enough to read on a phone (x-height about 31 px at the end). When the results page arrives (Enter at 3.53 s, the results in by 3.88 s) the camera drifts down and a little left (`drift`, 3.35-4.55 s, eased in and out) until the invented result 'Is this contest legitimate?' sits at y 550 with its start at x 260, clear of the caption band, and holds; the focus racks from the query to that line over the same move (3.5-4.4 s). At the hold the left edge shows a sliver of the laptop's bezel, as the email's end does. Review 10 (fault 8): the grey rounded bars (a source bar above each title, a second bar under each snippet, the tab row, the side column's blocks) read as a page still loading. screen.html now sets dim generic text where they were: a plain topic path above each title (no site, no domain), a line of dates and counts under each snippet, words in the tabs; the focus band keeps them as soft as the bars were. The side column moved right (its words from texture x 1236) so no word of it is ever cut by the frame's right edge, which reaches x 1219 at most once the results are in and 1097 at the hold. Nothing names a real service or says anything about the case; 'Is this contest legitimate?' stays the rack's sharp line.
